verified.pArithmetic: P(at least $100 in month 1) = P(a season is live and open to new entrants) x P(reaching a paid rank) x P(the payout is at least $100). Live evidence puts P(season live) at about 0.15 at most: Karma shows 0 open programs, the claim site is dead and the Celo docs omit it. If the claimed $5k/50 split held, the mean would be $100 per project. Payouts ranked by activity are usually skewed toward the top, so the median is probably below $100, and a newcomer with no Celo mainnet contract or onchain history would start low: P(ranked and paid) about 0.5, P(payout at least $100 | paid) about 0.4. 0.15 x 0.5 x 0.4 = 0.03. This is below the 10% bar, and the claimed 0.3 does not survive.
verified.nextAction: None now. Recheck karmahq.org/celo/funding-opportunities once a quarter. Reopen only if a named Proof of Ship season appears there with a stated pool and dates.
verified.evidenceQuotes: karmahq.org/celo/funding-opportunities: 'Open programs: 0 accepting now'; 'No matching programs ... More opportunities are on the way. Try other filters or check back later.' Karma GAP guide: 'a monthly contest'; 'impact metrics in your Karma project profile are used to automatically calculate builder rewards'; required inputs are GitHub repos, smart contract addresses, a payout address, a Divvi profile ID, a video of 4 min or less and 10 slides or fewer. celo.builderscore.xyz: 'certificate has expired'. docs.celo.org/build-on-celo/fund-your-project: lists only Prezenti Grants and Verda Ventures.

critic.why: The program is shut down: Talent was acquired and ended its rewards (post dated 2026-08-19), and the earn pages return 404. It also paid individual builders, not the MB, and bottom-tier payouts were trivial. This is the same dead program family as Celo Proof of Ship, so the two are duplicates in effect.

critic.name: Base Builder Grants
critic.why: Today's P is about 0.03 because the team has nothing on Base, and the grant requires 'actively building on Base'. Even in the best case (ShelterSplit on Base mainnet plus a Mini App with real USDC volume), the estimate is 0.08 to 0.10, which still doesn't clearly clear 10%. That estimate uses invented inputs (0.5 x 0.15-0.2), because Base publishes no applicant or award numbers. The 1-5 ETH figure is stale (from 2023). WATCH is justified only as a conditional lead after a deployment; it shares that trigger with both Circle items. The $5k cap is fine because it is a non-dilutive grant.

critic.name: Circle Developer Bounties (via DoraHacks)
critic.why: The only evidence is a 2024 round. No 2026 group could be verified: DoraHacks returned 405 and the Circle pages return 404. The 15% historical approval rate doesn't carry over to today. The bounties are narrow SDK tasks worth about 1,500 USDC and fit a game project poorly.

critic.name: Circle Alliance Program
critic.why: This is a business-development directory with no grant, prize or cash, so it fails the grants-only rule by definition. WATCH is the wrong verdict for something that can never pay. The team also isn't eligible without a live Circle integration. Its only value is credibility for Circle Developer Grants, and that item already covers it.

critic.name: Circle Developer Grants (adjacent lead found while verifying)
critic.why: Live and rolling, but none of the focus areas (agentic, FX, P2P payments, treasury, prediction markets, lending) covers gaming, NFTs or charity. It prioritizes Arc, and ShelterSplit isn't deployed anywhere. The 0.2 x 0.25 estimate uses guessed inputs, since there are no public stats, no disclosed amounts, and no geography or entity rules. The 10 to 15% figure applies only after an Arc deployment with real USDC flow. Its trigger is the same ShelterSplit mainnet deployment as Base Builder Grants, so treat the two as one pipeline gated on that deployment, not two independent chances.

critic.name: Anima International AI x Animal Welfare team
critic.why: This is not a funding program: the page offers no grants, and the claim of a funder network is false. The only money it mentions goes the other way (it asks readers to donate to Sentient Futures).

critic.name: Falcon Fund (Manifund)
critic.why: There is no inbound application form, and the manager sources grantees himself. The thesis is AI-model and policy work for animal welfare. None of the visible grantees is a consumer, game or companion-animal project. The 0.8% estimate was rounded up to 2% without justification, so 1% is closer. The only contact listed is a personal email, which must not be used or recorded.

critic.name: The Digital PawPrint newsletter
critic.why: This is media, not funding, and it looks dormant (latest issue Feb 2026). The 9% press-coverage estimate doesn't matter under the grants-only rule.

intro:
# Token Tails: warm-intro and inbound-discovery system (checked 2026-09-28, WebFetch only)

**Verdict up front:** this system finds people and opens conversations. It is not a funding source, and none of the channels below counts as an open grant. I checked every funding program the channels lead to. Only one, **Circle Grants**, clears "live, remote, non-equity and fits the team", and even for Circle I can't show P>10% with real numbers because its page gives no amounts and no acceptance rate. Everything else was **REFUTED** or **UNVERIFIED**, with reasons in the tables. Budget about 15 minutes of human review a day.

## 0. Checks that changed the plan

| Claim in the brief | What the live page shows | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Optimism gov forum "Missions" | `gov.optimism.io/categories.json` lists Missions only as "ARCHIVED & OLD Missions" (id 63). Grants moved to atlas.optimism.io. The Grants category (id 87) has 5 topics, all infrastructure (security proxy, calldata compression). | Missions is **REFUTED**. Watch the Grants RSS only, at low priority. |
| Arbitrum forum "grant" tag | `/tag/grant.rss` returns 404. The real tag is `grants-ecosystem`: 14 topics, newest from Jun 2026. `game-development-and` has 1 topic, the 2024 Gaming Catalyst proposal. | Gaming grants on Arbitrum are dormant. Arbitrum Gaming Ventures (AGV) is a venture vehicle, so it is excluded. |
| Base as a grant source | docs.base.org lists Base Batches ("$100K investment"; batch 004 closed Sep 10, 2026), the Base Ecosystem Fund (pre-seed and seed investment with Coinbase Ventures), and the Creators Grant (for content creators). | Nothing on Base is eligible. /base-builds is still useful for visibility only. |
| Gitcoin | `/campaigns` shows GG24 (Oct 2025) as the last regular round. The only ongoing items are TheDAO Security Fund and Protocol Guild. No GG25 is listed. | **REFUTED** for now. Watch for a GG25 announcement. |
| Celo forum Founders category | `/c/founders/42.rss` has 3 topics since 2024, the newest from Jun 2026. | Dead. Watch `latest.rss` instead, which is active (posts Sep 15–25, 2026, including "ArcadeX… live on Celo & MiniPay"). |
| Karma GAP | It now redirects to karmahq.org, which sells grant-management software. `/for-projects` still offers a free public profile, and `/funding-map` is live (for example, EF Local Meetups LATAM ends Dec 31, 2026). None of the listed programs fit a game team. | Keep the free profile. It is the credibility page funders click. |
| Circle | `circle.com/grants` is live. It pays tiered USDC tied to milestones, says "not equity", and prioritises Arc plus use cases such as P2P payments. You apply at circle.questbook.app, but that page rendered empty for me. | The only fitting live program. Whether it is open right now is **UNVERIFIED**. |
| Reddit | Both `www.reddit.com` and `old.reddit.com` are blocked for WebFetch. | **UNVERIFIED**. Use it for players only, never counted as a funding channel. |

## 1. Signal sources and how to watch them

P(reply) is my estimate of a substantive reply per well-targeted post or reply, not the chance of money.

| # | Source (verified) | Signal to watch | Automation (confirmed endpoint) | P(reply) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Celo forum, `https://forum.celo.org/latest.rss` | New games or MiniPay launches, Celo Public Goods funding requests, "builders" posts | RSS, valid, items Sep 2026. Also `categories.json` (Ecosystem id 25, Developers id 32) | 10–15% (small forum; staff answer MiniPay posts) |
| 2 | Farcaster /celo, `api.farcaster.xyz/v1/channel?channelId=celo` | Calls for MiniPay mini-apps; demo days | Channel metadata JSON works without a key (1,296 followers, 28 members, public casting on). Cast feeds need Neynar `GET /v2/farcaster/feed/channels/` with an API key; I couldn't load Neynar pricing. | 10–20% |
| 3 | Farcaster /base-builds | "What are you building" threads; Base staff amplifying demos | 54,549 followers, **public casting disabled** (invite via rounds.wtf/base-builds). Same Neynar feed. | 5% for amplification; about 0% for grants (Base funding is equity) |
| 4 | Farcaster /founders | Scouts asking for projects | 234,822 followers, public casting on | 2–5% |
| 5 | Farcaster /gamedev | Other game builders | 260 followers, 16 members | Low; peers only |
| 6 | Arbitrum forum, `/tag/grants-ecosystem.rss` and `/latest.rss` | New DAO grant programs, RFPs, audit subsidies | Both RSS valid. latest has posts Sep 16–23, 2026 | 3–5% |
| 7 | Arbitrum Foundation, `arbitrum.foundation/grants` | Audit Program ($10M ARB, subsidises third-party audits) could cover the ShelterSplit audit. It is **in-kind**, so it is not counted as funding. | Weekly page diff | n/a |
| 8 | Optimism gov, `https://gov.optimism.io/c/grants/87.rss` | Builder Grant proposals and council cycles | RSS valid (Sep 4, 2026 newest) | 2% (infrastructure focus) |
| 9 | Karma, `karmahq.org/funding-map` | New rounds tagged gaming, consumer or impact | Page diff. The OpenAPI file lists `GET /v2/programs`, but `gapapi.karmahq.xyz/v2/programs` returned 404, so the JSON endpoint is **UNVERIFIED** | n/a (discovery only) |
| 10 | Gitcoin, `gitcoin.co/campaigns` | A GG25 announcement | Page diff | n/a until a round exists |
| 11 | Manifund, `manifund.org/causes` | Animal welfare cause has 115 projects; the only active round is Falcon Fund | Page diff. No RSS found | Under 5%. EA regrantors mostly fund farmed-animal work, not companion animals. |
| 12 | EA Forum, `forum.effectivealtruism.org/feed.xml?view=tagRelevance&tagId=QdH9f8TC6G8oGYdgt` (animal welfare, sorted by relevance) plus `feed.xml?view=community-rss&karmaThreshold=2` (all new posts, Sep 27, 2026) | Funding calls from animal-welfare funders or organisations | RSS valid. Filter the all-posts feed by keyword, because the tag feed is not sorted by date | Under 3% for money; 10% for feedback |
| 13 | r/gamedev, r/IndieDev showcase threads | Player feedback only | **UNVERIFIED** (blocked). Reddit's public `.rss` is the usual method. | n/a for funding |
| 14 | Discord grant channels (Celo, Arbitrum, Circle developers) | Office hours, grant announcements | **UNVERIFIED.** WebFetch can't read them. Join by hand, and forward announcement channels into the same digest with a bot you control. | 10–20% in office hours |

**X keyword searches** (the same text works in X search, rss.app and twitterapi.io; add `since_time:<unix>` on the API):

1. `("looking for projects" OR "looking for builders" OR "calling all builders") (grant OR grants OR funding) -filter:replies lang:en`
2. `("we're funding" OR "we are funding" OR "now funding") (games OR gaming OR "mini apps") -filter:replies`
3. `("DM me" OR "reply with") ("building on" OR "what are you building") (cats OR pets OR "animal welfare" OR shelter)`
4. `(RFP OR "request for proposals") (Celo OR MiniPay OR Arbitrum OR USDC OR Arc) -filter:replies`
5. `("grant program" OR "grants round" OR "builder grants") (consumer OR games OR "social impact") -filter:replies min_faves:5`
6. `("animal welfare" OR "animal shelter" OR rescue) (web3 OR onchain OR USDC OR stablecoin)`
7. `(MiniPay "mini app" OR "minipay games") -filter:replies`
8. `(from:circle OR from:arc) (grant OR builders OR "office hours")` (confirm the official handles by hand)
9. `("show me your" OR "drop your") (game OR "web game" OR "browser game") -filter:replies`
10. `("office hours" OR "demo day") (Celo OR Arbitrum OR Circle) builders`

**Pipeline** (no servers):
- A GitHub Actions cron runs every 6 hours. It pulls feeds 1, 6, 8 and 12 and the twitterapi.io searches, and diffs the Karma, Gitcoin, Manifund and Arbitrum grants pages.
- It removes items already seen (by guid or tweet id), then an LLM scores each item from 0 to 3 on "asks for projects AND fits games/cats/USDC".
- Items scoring 2 or more go into one daily digest email, with a pre-filled reply draft from the templates in section 4.
- The human's only job is to approve or edit and post the reply. No auto-posting, which avoids X spam flags and the rule against contacting people automatically.

## 2. Monitoring X without the paid official API

| Option | Live check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| nitter.net | ECONNREFUSED | Dead |
| xcancel.com | HTTP 451 | Blocked |
| rss.app | Pricing: free tier is 2 feeds, 5 posts, 24h refresh; Basic $8.32/mo for 15 feeds at 60 min; Developer $16.64/mo for 100 feeds at 15 min. Its marketing says X search and hashtag feeds work, but it states no reliability terms. | Works, but you pay a flat fee and reliability is unproven |
| twitterapi.io | "$0.15 per 1K tweets", "Minimum $0.00015 (15 Credits) per API call", "no minimum spend", no free credits. Advanced search is `GET /twitter/tweet/advanced_search` with queryType Latest or Top and up to 20 results per page. | **Cheapest reliable option** |

twitterapi.io arithmetic for 10 queries every 6 hours (4 runs a day):
- Calls: 10 × 4 × 30 = 1,200 calls a month.
- Worst case, every call returns a full page of 20 tweets: 1,200 × 20 = 24,000 tweets a month, at $0.15 per 1,000 = **$3.60/mo**.
- Floor, if no calls return tweets: 1,200 × $0.00015 = $0.18/mo.
- At 15 queries every 3 hours it is still under $11/mo.

That beats rss.app Basic ($8.32 for 15 feeds at 60 min). Use the rss.app free tier (2 feeds) as a fallback for the two most important queries.

## 3. Warm-intro paths (public roles and the shared surface to meet them on)

| Target role | Shared surface | Method | P(reply) | Funding reachable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circle developer relations / grants team | Circle developer Discord office hours (UNVERIFIED), replies to Circle and Arc builder posts (query 8), circle.questbook.app | Deploy ShelterSplit on an Arc testnet first. Then reply to a builder call with "USDC P2P payouts to shelters, tested contract, demo". Ask which grant tier fits. | 15–25% | Circle Grants: live, milestone USDC, not equity. Amounts not disclosed. |
| Celo / MiniPay ecosystem lead or DevRel | /celo Farcaster (public casting), Celo forum Ecosystem post, MiniPay builder calls | Publish a "Token Tails on MiniPay" forum post with a demo GIF, and cast it in /celo. Staff reply to MiniPay launches (ArcadeX got a thread on Sep 24). | 15–20% | Celo Public Goods: celopg.eco didn't render, so **UNVERIFIED** |
| Base builder or ecosystem team | /base-builds (needs invite), replies on "what are you building" | Visibility only | 5% | Nothing eligible (equity only) |
| Arbitrum Foundation grants or audit program manager | forum `grants-ecosystem`, governance calls (Sep 22 call listed) | Ask about the Audit Program for ShelterSplit. In-kind only. | 5–10% | Audit subsidy, not cash |
| Animal-welfare tech (shelter software staff, rescue digital leads, EA animal-welfare authors) | EA Forum comments on relevant posts, the shelter's own public adoption channels | Offer a free 30-day feature of their adoptable cats, with a click report | 10–20% from shelters, under 3% from EA funders | None directly. The value is shelter partners, which funders ask about. |
| Karma profile visitors (any grant reviewer) | karmahq.org project profile | Keep milestones current: ShelterSplit tests, deploy, first payout | n/a | Makes every other application more credible |

**P>10% check for funding through this system:**
- Circle: roughly P(apply) 1.0 × P(accepted). Circle publishes no acceptance rate and names Arc alignment as a priority. Accepted odds are maybe 10–20% after an Arc deployment and 5% or less without one. So it sits at the bar and is not proven.
- Every other path: P(money) is under 5%, or the programme is excluded or equity.
- **Recommendation:** build the monitor, since it costs about $4 a month and 15 minutes a day. Put the real effort into one path: the Circle/Arc deployment, then the Circle grant application.

## 4. Message templates (each under 90 words; no token-sale language; placeholders for all numbers)

**A. X reply to a call-for-projects (61 words)**
> Token Tails fits this: free browser games (Phaser, no install) whose characters are AI-drawn portraits of real shelter cats. Each cat is linked to its shelter, and our ShelterSplit contract pays that shelter in USDC automatically (41 Foundry tests, testnet today). Demo: {demo_url}. {players} players so far. Happy to share the repo or a 2-minute walkthrough.

**B. Cold DM or email to an ecosystem lead (79 words)**
> Hi {name}, I saw your {post/office_hours} about {program}. We build Token Tails: casual browser games where each playable cat is a real shelter cat, and a ShelterSplit Solidity contract routes USDC to that shelter. It is tested (41 Foundry tests) but not yet on mainnet. We'd like to deploy it on {chain} and run a {n}-shelter pilot. Would a 15-minute look at the demo ({demo_url}) be worthwhile, or is there a better program or person for this? Repo: {repo_url}.

**C. Pitch to an animal-welfare organisation (78 words)**
> Hello {org} team, we make Token Tails, free browser games starring real adoptable shelter cats, drawn from your photos with your permission. Players meet {cat_name}, see your adoption link, and a share of what players spend on that cat goes to you, paid via {payout_method}. It costs you nothing and needs no crypto knowledge. Could we feature {n} of your cats for a free 30-day trial and send you a report of clicks to your adoption page?

Before sending C, check that {payout_method} and the revenue share match what ShelterSplit actually does.
